sources.title: Simon Board and Moritz Meyer-ter-Vehn, Writing Economic Theory Papers
sources.actual_version: October 2018 on actual first page; seven-page author-hosted PDF. Do not substitute the October2014 version surfaced by a search index.
sources.actual_reading: All seven physical pages read as extracted text. Used contribution/model-purpose discussion1–3, explicit model primitives4–5 and theorem/proof/intuition/implication architecture6–7. Physical pages have no printed page numbers.
sources.supports: A stated economic question, transparent model primitives and qualified contribution; separating theorem, proof and interpretation.
limits: Methodological advice, not a theorem proving external validity or a universal publication standard. No quoted examples or economic results from the cited papers are imported.
The chapter independently proves all original models and does not adopt guidance to avoid substantive criticism, suppress necessary proof detail, or treat journal tastes as mathematical evidence.
sources.retrieval_note: The UCLA department resource page links the HTTPS URL, whose web/open and urllib attempt timed out. The exact author-hosted HTTP route returned the retained PDF; actual local body and page image were then inspected.

sources.title: Jonathan B. Berk, Campbell R. Harvey and David Hirshleifer, Preparing a Referee Report: Guidelines and Perspectives
sources.actual_version: February17,2015 on actual physical/printed1. Seven pages; PDF modification metadata in2016 is not its stated authorship date. This is not the related2017 JEP article.
sources.actual_reading: All seven physical/printed pages read in official web text; local text retained. Used role and scope2, summary/cover letter/report3, supported major versus optional comments4–5, proportionality/evidence and avoiding endless requests6–7.
sources.supports: A referee’s concise contribution summary, evidence for consequential objections, distinction between required repair and optional extension, and proportionate follow-up.
limits: Authors’ dated methodological guidance is not a current binding journal policy. Do not inherit prestige thresholds, rejection-rate assertions, a one-counterexample-only convention or automatic rejection from a correctable error.
The teaching rubric assesses validity and relevance without claiming actual publication quality, external human certification, or a predetermined policy view.

original_work: All six models, twelve exact transfer questions/solutions, fictional submission, report, proofs and numerical results are original instructional work. The two method guides support narrowly attributed writing/referee practices, not the correctness or economic realism of these models.
runtime_boundary: Only canonical HTML/checker/source/author JSON are required at runtime; preparation, blueprint and retained sources are provenance only.
excluded_claims: Theoretical implication, equilibrium selection, empirical discrimination and welfare normalization are separate claims.
No general identification theorem, infinite-dimensional existence, generic robust optimization or institutional implementation guarantee.
The six cases and twelve transfers are original instructional constructions; methodology sources do not certify their economic realism or research importance.
